figures.caption: Figure 1. Detection speed and candidate boundaries at the nominal setting. Retained peaks propose four components in 18–21 s and three in 30–33 s; red dotted lines mark intervening speed minima.

Figure 2. Overview of the final method. Speed structure proposes the count and intervals; timing and displacement are fitted, then evaluated against matched-count uniform baselines and parameter sensitivity.

Figure 3. First-window XYZ position and velocity comparison at K=4. The fitted trajectory reduces average position error but introduces a sharp velocity excursion near the high-speed candidate boundary.

Figure 4. Second-window XYZ position and velocity comparison at K=3. The method captures the major Y and Z movement better than the same-count controls but still misses the X-position excursion and some earlier details.

Figure 5. Position and velocity errors across distinct speed-based partitions and uniform baselines at the same K. Stars mark the nominal proposals. Changing prominence changes both count and boundaries, so this is not a count-only causal comparison.

Figure 6. Timing-neighborhood sensitivity with fixed counts and candidate boundaries. Narrow, nominal and wide use (α,β)=(0.30,0.10), (0.45,0.20) and (0.60,0.30), respectively. The vertical scales differ between windows.

scope: Current author-formatted report, joint-objective supplement and author-exported PDF reviewed.
